chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who claims that a man's slave is his son: 'He is freed from the property of the one who claimed him. If the claimant dies and his property is distributed before the slave is freed, the property has preceded him [i.e., the slave's manumission is paid from the estate], and if he is freed before his property is distributed, then he has his share from it [i.e., the slave retains his share of the estate].'

key_terms.سَبَقَهُ اَلْمَالُ: The property preceded him (estate covers the cost)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a slave claimed as a son if the claimant dies before the slave is freed?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) establishes the principle of 'al-'itq min al-mal' (manumission from the estate), ensuring the claimant's financial responsibility for the slave's freedom is settled before inheritance distribution. It highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the priority of debt-like obligations (manumission costs) versus inheritance shares, a concept further elaborated by later scholars like Al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
